subject: general
question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.

The more __enlightened__ employers offer better terms.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option (3) i.e. Confounded**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"enlightened"** means having or showing a rational, modern, and well-informed outlook; free from ignorance, prejudice, or superstition. (प्रबुद्ध)

 
 
• **Example: **Enlightened leaders always seek ways to improve the welfare of their people.
 
 
 
• **"Confounded" **refers to being confused, bewildered, or perplexed. (भ्रमित)
 
 
• **Example: **She was confounded by the sudden and unexpected turn of events.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'enlightened' is 'confounded'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option (3) i.e. Confounded**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Civilised** (सभ्य): Polite and well-mannered; associated with social and cultural advancement.

 
 
• **Example:** The debate remained civilised despite the participants' differing opinions.
 
 
 
• **Educated** (शिक्षित): Having acquired knowledge and intellectual development, especially through formal schooling.
 
 
• **Example: **The educated workforce is crucial for the nation's development.
 
 
 
• **Reasonable** (उचित): Fair, sensible, and logical.
 
 
• **Example:** It is reasonable to expect timely feedback on work projects.
